overview: Two non-Mendelian inheritance patterns where heterozygotes don't simply show the dominant trait, but the resulting phenotype differs in an important way.
genZNote: Incomplete dominance blends the paint. Codominance keeps both colors separate, side by side.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A pattern in which the heterozygote phenotype is an intermediate blend between the two homozygous phenotypes.
aspects.valueB: A pattern in which both alleles are fully and separately expressed in the heterozygote, with neither masking the other.

aspects.label: Heterozygote Phenotype
aspects.valueA: A blended, intermediate phenotype (e.g. pink flowers from red and white parents).
aspects.valueB: Both parental phenotypes appear simultaneously and distinctly (e.g. AB blood type showing both A and B antigens).

aspects.label: Classic Example
aspects.valueA: Snapdragon flower color: red x white = pink.
aspects.valueB: ABO blood group: IA and IB alleles are codominant, producing type AB blood.

aspects.label: Molecular Basis
aspects.valueA: Often reflects partial function/dosage effects of a single gene product (e.g. half the normal amount of pigment).
aspects.valueB: Reflects two distinct, independently functioning gene products both being produced and detectable.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Traits blend into an intermediate phenotype.
aspects.valueB: Both traits appear fully and separately, without blending.
